title: Cush (Nubia)
lead: Cush is the Bible's name for the lands south of Egypt along the upper Nile (Nubia, in modern Sudan), which the Greek Bible calls Ethiopia. Cushites appear as a far-off people, as soldiers in Egypt's armies, as a ruling dynasty of Egypt (the Twenty-fifth Dynasty), and as individuals in Israel's story.

sections.b: Cush is a son of Ham (Genesis 10:6–8), and the Gihon river "circles the whole land of Cush" (Genesis 2:13). Moses married a Cushite woman (Numbers 12:1). A Cushite runner brought David the news of Absalom's death (2 Samuel 18:21–32). Zerah the Cushite invaded Judah under Asa (2 Chronicles 14:9–15), and Tirhakah king of Cush marched against Sennacherib (2 Kings 19:9). The prophets name Cush as the far edge of the world (Isaiah 18:1–7; Zephaniah 3:10), Ebed-melech the Cushite rescued Jeremiah (Jeremiah 38:7–13), and Philip baptized an "Ethiopian" official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians (Acts 8:27), that is, the Kandake of Meroë in Cush.
